title: Introduce CUDA-graph telemetry and rollback hooks for replay regressions
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds optional telemetry and automatic rollback hooks for CUDA-graph replay to detect and mitigate capture/replay-induced latency regressions. Feature is behind a runtime flag and gated in Dedicated/Private by default. Impact: safer rollout of graph reuse, improved visibility into replay failures and warmup regressions.
description:
Motivation:
CUDA-graph capture/replay gives large throughput benefits, but we see intermittent warmup regressions and shape/kernel mismatches that cause 95/99p latency spikes or correctness fallbacks. This PR introduces two defensive layers: (1) fine-grained telemetry and fingerprinting around captures/replay to detect regressions quickly, and (2) a configurable rollback hook that automatically disables graph reuse for a given model/pool/shape when a regression signature is observed.

What this PR does (single-string description):
- Add capture/replay telemetry: histograms for capture time, replay time, kernel-switch events, fallback counts, and shape-fingerprint occurrence. Telemetry emitted with tags: model, pool_id, device_family, capture_signature.
- Implement capture signatures: lightweight fingerprinting of op sequence + tensor shape vector + quantization flags used to match ambiguous shape-guard cases without over-constraining graphs.
- Rollback hooks: policy engine that observes telemetry windows and triggers a rollback action (disable_graph_reuse) for the affected pool/model/shape if thresholds are exceeded (configurable: latency_pct_increase, fallback_rate, error_count). Rollbacks are rate-limited and recorded to audit logs.
- KV-cache warmup probe: a background probe that runs a small set of priming requests after rollback before attempting a new capture to avoid repeated capture failures due to cold KV state. The probe is conservative and capped per-minute.
- Continuous batching integration: graph reuse decision now considers current batch size distribution probe so that fragmentation-heavy workloads don't get aggressive reuse.
- Runtime config: new flags (cudagraph.telemetry.enabled, cudagraph.rollback.enabled, cudagraph.rollback.latency_pct, cudagraph.rollback.min_samples, cudagraph.probe.kv_warmup_enabled) with sane defaults documented in docs/ and safe off-by-default for hosted tier.
- Tests & benchmarks: unit tests for signature computation and rollback policy, integration test simulating warmup regression, and a perf microbenchmark that shows median throughput unchanged and 99p reduced in flagged regressions.

Diff summary (high level):
- runtime/cudagraph/telemetry.rs (new): telemetry primitives and exporters (histograms, tags).
- runtime/cudagraph/signature.rs (new): capture signature computation and serialization.
- runtime/cudagraph/rollback.rs (new): policy engine, decision logic, backoff, and audit hooks.
- runtime/scheduler/graph_manager.rs (modifications): plumb telemetry and rollback decisions into capture/replay path.
- runtime/kv/cache_probe.rs (new): KV warmup probe and limiter.
- tests/integration/cudagraph_regression_test.rs (new): end-to-end test that injects synthetic kernel slowdowns.
- docs/configuration/cudagraph.md (update): explains flags and safe rollout steps.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed in ENG-7321
- [x] Unit and integration tests added
- [x] Perf microbenchmarks run and attached
- [x] Runtime flags added and documented
- [x] Rollout plan in PR description

Testing & Benchmarks:
- CI: all unit/integration tests pass (see ci_checks below).
- Local perf: on p4d-like hardware, enabling telemetry+rollback against a workload with an injected kernel slowdown reduces 99p latency from 1.8s to 0.62s by disabling graph reuse for the offending signature and falling back to streaming path; median throughput remained within 3% of baseline.
- Canary: initial canary in dedicated-us-west with feature flag off-by-default; gradual enablement via automated Linear workflow.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main behind feature flags (telemetry.enabled=false by default for hosted).
2) Enable telemetry in dedicated canaries (non-disruptive).
3) Monitor telemetry for 72h and enable rollback.enabled for selected pools with conservative thresholds.
4) Iterate on thresholds and expand.

Backwards compatibility and safety:
- All hooks are opt-in via runtime config.
- Rollbacks are rate-limited and emitted as auditable actions; manual override allowed.
- No changes to model formats or on-disk artifacts.

Notes for reviewers:
- The signature algorithm is intentionally conservative — it may under-partition shapes to avoid excessive graph churn. See signature.rs comments for rationale.
- Telemetry labels are calibrated to be low-cardinality; we add an optional high-cardinality debug sink behind a different flag for investigations.

End of description.

review_comments: Ethan Varga: Please add an explicit test for rate-limiting so we don't trigger oscillation during noisy bursts. -> addressed in commit 4.
